parsed.explanation: The dossier documents a tier-1 national exposure: the federal passport regime now issues markers by assigned sex, has eliminated X markers, and a February 2025 cable instructs officers to refuse applications where documents 'cast reasonable doubt' on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility — a universal-exposure rule every trans or nonbinary visitor meets at the visa/passport gate. Foreign governments have issued travel advisories after detentions of foreign trans citizens over visa issues, so the exposure demonstrably reaches visitors. Partially criminalised facility bans exist in some states (one documented trespass arrest), and immigration custody shows severe abuse, though some claims rest on a single source. Mitigants: courts have blocked several orders and the passport policy is under challenge; roughly half the states have no facility ban; hate-crime and employment protections exist; no organised physical targeting of visitors is documented and no violence rate appears. This matches the 0.45 anchor: universal, partially unremedied federal document/facility exposure with uneven subnational regimes and working but contested recourse.
